# CHD-3.2 Part II — render record (sections 5-8)
Ticket: t_a9280086 (render Part II). Sources: `build-spec/VOL-B`, `VOL-C`, `VOL-E`, `VOL-A` §4.3, `contracts/ENDPOINTS.md`. Generator: `handbook/gen-p2.py` + `p2base.py` + `p2_s5..p2_s8.py`.

## Verification performed
- `render.sh` exit 0 on all four files; per-page fit from `data-fit-all` (all inside 4.5-9.7 mm). - `check.py` on each PDF: A4, 2 colours (pure black on white), allowed fonts only, 300 dpi tiles under `handbook/tiles-chd32/`. - `p2_qa.py` (geometric): 0 findings on all 21 pages — no text out of the 179 mm column, no text-on-text overlap, no word crossing a rule or a figure box edge, no clipped thumb tab. - Placeholder grep over the four sources: zero `[BRACKETED]`, `TBD`, `TODO`, `lorem`. - Figure/table id claims: every id above appears as a caption in exactly one file; the only external hit is `FIGURE 8.1-1` inside the section-16 traceability register, which cites it. - Figure substance checks (vision on 150-170 dpi crops, defects fixed and re-checked): - FIGURE 5.2-1: bond column given real boxes so no arrowhead ended in space; row 2 (REUSE) no longer draws a provisioning box, so the dashed bypass cannot strike the word NONE. - FIGURE 5.3-1: barred end for the stored-only delayed reply now stops 4.6 mm short of the manager lifeline; the roll-up self-message and its label share one lane; roots 41/43 stated as owned by b-M so reply routing is unambiguous. - FIGURE 6.2-1: DONE moved outside the non-terminal panel; T7 routed REWORK -> IN_PROGRESS (was wrongly REWORK -> BLOCKED); every edge carries its transition number; T5 label clear of the panel border. - FIGURE 6.3-1: dependency edge routed below the sibling boxes; barred at the cancelled prerequisite; export/import routed around the ticket boxes. - FIGURE 7.2-1: 4x5 key grid rebuilt after an initial 3-column grid overflowed its panel; the archive namespace given matching boxes; the "also in this namespace" note moved inside its panel; `<id>` normalised to `<ticket-id>`. - FIGURE 8.1-1: redrawn as ONE dashed service boundary holding contract surface, writer and store; the WAKE edge now leaves the SINGLE WRITER box (it previously attached to the boundary, which read as store-to-gateway); the scheduler box was removed because its callback edge could not be routed without crossing the door column - the callback is printed in TABLE 8.1-2 and §8.1 instead.

## Content the acceptance names explicitly
- Message-kind enum with per-role legality: TABLE 5.1-2 (seven values). - Transition matrix: TABLE 6.2-1, state-for-state identical to FIGURE 6.2-1 (T1-T8). - Cancelled prerequisite is drawn barred and labelled NOT SATISFIED, and TABLE 6.3-1 prints the outcome table (R31-009). - Field registries: TABLE 6.1-1 (TicketRecord), 5.2-3 (SendManifest), 5.4-1 (SessionBond). - Error catalog with status + machine code + retryability: TABLE 8.3-1 (19 rows). - Attachment support matrix: TABLE 8.3-2. - Agent -> service -> DuckBrain path with the service boundary visible and no agent-to-store edge: FIGURE 8.1-1 plus the two posture lines beneath it.

## Open items for the merge/index ticket
1. Leaf numbers. The generator derives the leaf base from the manifest: the page count of every earlier section's `files:` on disk. Sections 1-4 are 21 pages (Part I), so sections 5-8 print LEAF 22-42 (5: 22-27, 6: 28-32, 7: 33-37, 8: 38-42). Part III printed leaves 30-40 and Part IV 41-55 against an assumed 8-sheet Part II; those two ranges are now stale and must be recomputed by the continuous-leaf merge pass (t_71fabd48). The leaf is print-order only and is never cited in prose. (Earlier in this ticket the base was read from a local file table and printed LEAF 1; fixed by reading the manifest instead - `p2base.leaf_base`.) 2. `gen-index.py` is not present on disk, so the manifest check could not be run from here; the YAML parses (yaml.safe_load) and the sections 5-8 registries match the printed ids. 3. Part II uses one multi-page file per section (the manifest's `files:`/`pdfs:` shape) rather than one file per sheet as Parts I/III/IV chose. `render.sh` only reports page 1, so every page was measured with pymupdf block extents and with the page's own fit script.
